simplified: Your dreams can help you understand things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being naked in public, usually mean similar things for many people. To understand what they mean for you, think about your daily life and feelings.

One interesting case of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets of Moscow. Some dogs were born wild, and some were pets that people left behind. Some dogs live alone, and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and saw that they have done very well in the city. They learned it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio, who lives in New York. She got the idea for the book after seeing a girl with a different face on the street. Wonder is very popular in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools use it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not normal pets, and she has told many people that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if you take care of them. She understands why some people don’t like them. Chloe also didn’t like rats until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats, and she saw how loving and smart they are. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided to get two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed by cars, and others have died from electric cables. Baboons are in danger of disappearing, so the city has hired Baboon Monitors. Their job is to move baboons away from the city or catch them and let them go in the countryside. This plan has worked a little, but it is still hard to keep baboons from returning to the city for food.

I work for a big IT company, but their main office is in the USA, so I do my work online from home. This helps me save time because I don’t have to travel or talk a lot with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this is good for me because I can take time off when my kids have school events or when I need to see the dentist. The problem is that I often work late into the evening and sometimes miss dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti was still popular, but street art became very popular around the world. Some artists wanted to show important ideas about war, unfairness, and discrimination. Other street artists just wanted to make pretty art. In South America, many street artists worked in poor areas to make grey city walls more colorful and beautiful.

Every day, social media, magazines, and store windows show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people wear a few times and then throw away.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw the dust from the car going to the Big House. The horses kicked at flies and did not care about their owner's visit after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter only came out when he needed to, which was good for Sam. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. The wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was getting red in the June sun. He looked like a man who made money while others worked.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs is very cruel, and there were strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Because of the protests, the city council chose to find a kinder way to deal with the pigs. They put up fences and made it against the law to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be hard because warmer winters mean there are more pigs now than before.

Suzanne was inspired to write the Hunger Games because she loves Greek myths. When she was a child, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, the city of Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As a punishment, the king of Crete makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The children are put in a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. But Theseus, one of the boys, fights and kills the Minotaur. Suzanne thinks of Katniss Everdeen as a modern Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing people and animals together. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or left behind as pets. Zoos also study how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend against buying too much is called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then came to the US. It is a way to say no to spending too much on Black Friday and Cyber Monday after Thanksgiving. On Buy Nothing Day, people protest and cut their credit cards. All year, Buy Nothing groups help people trade and fix things they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many places, writing or painting on walls that are not yours is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some had to pay money. Many city leaders say it costs a lot to clean graffiti from buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? More and more people see it as real art. There have been big shows of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald made a street art show in a New York gallery. She said that street artists are just sharing their feelings and not hurting anyone. They should be liked and celebrated.

Most people have four to six dreams every night after they turn ten. This means they can have about 2,000 dreams each year. By the time they are 80 years old, a person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget most of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand in our lives. It is easy to think that sometimes a dream can happen in real life, especially if the dream is about something we see often.

The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America is destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor areas ruled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has all the power. Each area makes different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives all the coal for the country. There was a thirteenth area, but it fought against the Capitol and was destroyed.

Wild animals sometimes come into cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons go into neighborhoods to eat. They open trash cans and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons even enter houses and steal food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have hurt many pets, so many people in the city do not like them.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make a mistake, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, and this can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first movie directors to use the 17 steps of the hero's journey in his stories. Usually, the hero starts with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the call to adventure that begins his journey.

One idea to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to blow it up with a nuclear bomb. This sounds like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon, but NASA really has a plan called HAMMER. They would shoot eight-ton rockets at the asteroid to change its path. If the asteroid is too close, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to explode it.

Campbell says that the hero first says no to the adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they choose to go into a special world for the adventure. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, the mentor is Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and the enemy is Darth Vader in the special world of the Death Star.

Some people think unused items are not helpful, but others find them valuable. With the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these items. Now, using websites and social media, it is easy to buy and sell second-hand things. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we do not know about ourselves. Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can learn about our hidden feelings and problems. The other idea was different. It said that dreams are just random thoughts in our brain while it organizes memories from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and make a story from them.

I am a freelancer and work for myself. This is good because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus because there were many distractions, like housework, tea, and my family needing me. So, I went to a café to work, but the Wi-Fi was not good and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I rented a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I liked getting ready for work in the morning and being able to concentrate in an office.

NASA needs money to build a special space telescope called NEOCam. This telescope will help find middle-sized asteroids. If NASA gets the money, it can find them in ten years. After that, the team will need to figure out how to protect Earth from dangerous asteroids.

The 'buy nothing' trend is now popular with social media influencers who usually show clothes and make-up for people to buy. Some YouTube stars tell their viewers not to buy anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. In the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. Then, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi cares about religion. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions. He becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. Pi surprises everyone by saying he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him choose his own religion.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have clear dreams. Clear dreams are when you know you are dreaming and can change what happens in the dream. This means you can change a scary dream into a nice one, or control the story of your dream like a movie director. Instead of just understanding your dreams, you will be making them, but you might still want some dreams that show you what you are thinking!

Some people do not know they help the problem of disposable clothes when they give their old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all these clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of style quickly and is often too bad to recycle; people do not want to buy it used. Many clothes are thrown away, and a lot that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, making more problems.

Some adventurers want more than one great trip. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the hot Sahara Desert. But her best trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into ice and needed help. Many people would stop there, but Meagan kept going. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sled with her tent and food through the cold and storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls in Paris. Now, he wants people to think about social problems. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to make residents think about homelessness.

In some places, local governments have asked artists to paint in special areas instead of on random walls. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint freely. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has let some artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys visiting different places. You can see her art on sidewalks, in empty factories, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned by city workers. For her, this shows that life is always changing with endings and new starts.

Gabriela used to work in a place where bosses had a lot of power and everyone respected them, but her Swedish team worked in a place where everyone, including the bosses, worked together to make decisions.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences with her team, she talked to them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share that they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she did not trust them. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to change her decisions, and they explained that this was how they always worked.

Os Gêmeos are twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint many things, like small tags and big, colorful pictures of people on buildings. Their art is so big that they need cranes to help them. In 2007, they painted a whole castle in Scotland.

People have painted and written on walls for a long time. In ancient times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include messages about religion, politics, love, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever wanted to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? If yes, you are not alone. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across countries. Today’s adventurers use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones, unlike explorers in the past who used maps and compasses. Many adventurers love nature and want to help people and raise money for charities.

The first test is called DART, which stands for Double Asteroid Redirection Test. They plan to test DART on a moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, called 'Didymoon', is 150 meters wide and goes around its bigger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that DART will hit it and change its path so that telescopes on Earth can see it.

The main character is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in an accident and needs to find food for her family. She hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and gets very good with a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is picked to go to the games, Katniss decides to go instead. The other person from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss starts to have a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details. Think about the people and places in your dream because they can help you understand it better. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. Now you can link your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

In the past, many bridges were made of wood and could easily catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could start a fire and burn the bridge down.

We cannot know how street art will change in the future, but we see some new trends. Many street artists are young people who paint in their cities, but now more artists are traveling and working in different countries. Some artists use the internet to connect and share pictures of their art. The art world is also starting to accept street art as real art. We may not know what will happen next, but street art is not going away!

Suzanne Collines has always felt sad when she saw news about wars. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and he fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to keep her safe by not telling her about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

A global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) asked over 40,000 young people and older people about work culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. Another survey by Deloitte had over 10,000 young people sharing their views on the challenges and chances in the work world.

Erik Weihenmayer is from the United States and loves adventures. He has ridden a bike in Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. He also helps people with disabilities to be active and takes young blind people climbing.
Online platforms let people earn some extra money easily. For example, busy parents can now sell their children's old clothes and baby items online instead of setting up a stall at a market.

Pi and Richard Parker stay in the lifeboat for 227 days. They feel hungry, sick, and very tired. They face strong storms and hot sun, but they survive. Sometimes, Pi feels better with his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. At last, he sees the Mexican coast, and everything changes. It is better to read the book to see what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. She had homework, but it could wait. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time before her parents came home and the house became noisy with talking, TV, or her dad listening to jazz while cooking. She liked this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's team found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1km wide. These are called 'near-Earth objects' or NEOs, and they are as big as mountains. They include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's path. NASA thinks there are about 50 more to find, but none of the 887 they know about are a big danger to Earth.

Auggie decides to go to school, but his first day is very hard. He feels nervous like every new student, but people stare at him because of how he looks. No one wants to sit with him. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack and Summer. However, his classmates are scared to touch him. Throughout the school year, Auggie has many good and bad moments until something surprising and upsetting happens at a school camp.

The two men looked at the north side of the land. It went on and on. They could hardly see the fences. A teenage boy might feel bored and want to run away, but he couldn't do it on foot. Sam looked at the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground. He wondered if the boy could ride. A good rider could find trouble out here, far from anyone. But someone who didn't know about horses might get into even more trouble trying to escape from his father.

More than 4,000 climbers, from 13 to 80 years old, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is very dangerous, but the best climbers want new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria loved climbing mountains when she was a teenager. After school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde wanted to climb all fourteen of the world's tallest mountains. To make it harder, she climbs without oxygen tanks. This is dangerous because there is less oxygen at the top of high mountains, which can be bad for the brain and body. Gerlinde helps a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal with her fame as a climber.

If we look at the things we have bought, we can see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we bought even though we live in a hot country, the old smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that became a storage room.

In history and in different cultures, people believed that dreams could tell the future. They thought dreams were messages from gods that gave us important information. Even now, many people remember dreaming about something that later happened in real life.

Many big and costly transportation projects in the world have built bridges. Bridges are important because they help cars, trucks, and trains cross water, mountains, or other roads. They are very important in civil engineering and people pay close attention to them, especially if they fall down.

After many weeks of problems, Gabriela wrote an email to her Swedish manager about her team. Her manager asked if she thought her team was doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and did not feel he was helping enough.

Dogs that live in groups know that humans often give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for everyone. Some dogs can even use the metro to move around their area! Scientists don’t know how dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to find their favorite places. Another idea is that they understand the names of stations from the announcements. Now, people on the metro see dogs so often that they hardly notice them.

Ed Stafford from the UK was the first person to walk the whole Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and finished at the river's end in Brazil, two years and four months later, after walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always in danger. Luckily, he only got many bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four per cent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two big problems for society and the environment. First, many people use credit cards to pay for these clothes. British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 per cent of what they spend on clothes. Also, people are spending money they do not have to buy things they do not need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothes every year, and most of it goes to landfills.

Ed's walk was only possible because of technology. He used a radio to ask people in the rainforest for food and to cross their land. Many people came to help him and showed him the best paths. While walking, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the attention from the media to talk about the damage to the rainforest and to collect money for charities in Brazil and Peru that help the environment and children.

Businesses have realized they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. Some companies now offer online platforms that connect customers with people who have products or services to share. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn extra money in their free time.

One important job of zoos today is to help breed endangered animals. In nature, some rare animals have trouble finding partners and having babies. They also face dangers from hunters, losing their homes, and other animals that hunt them. A good zoo helps these animals live and breed safely. When wild animal numbers go down, they can become too similar. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo animals to go back to the wild and make the population stronger.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can make a bridge fall for different reasons. Trains can make a bridge fall because they hit it very hard. Boats can make a bridge fall because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to stop bridges from falling is to plan ahead. New technology that finds weak spots, safer work areas, and better designs can help prevent these bad accidents.

At first, Pi is very scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water, so he climbs back into the lifeboat. The animals in the lifeboat start to kill and eat each other until only Pi and a tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, which he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right now.

When Pi is 16, a new government is chosen that his parents do not like. They are worried about the future, so they decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family takes the animals with them on a ship to Canada. During the trip, there is a big storm and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi is in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a big tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teens and young adults by the American writer Suzanne Collins. It came out in 2008 and has been translated into 26 languages, selling millions of copies worldwide. It was the first book for young readers to sell over a million e-books. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is also very successful, making 152.5 million dollars in its first weekend in North America!

Dreams might happen because our mind is putting together our thoughts from the day, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we think mostly in words, like talking to ourselves. But when we sleep, the part of our brain for language works less, and the part for feelings works more.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. A study showed that happy people have strong connections with friends and family, and they spend time with them often. You also need at least one person to share your feelings with. Just one close friend is enough, along with other friends. It’s not enough to have many friends just to have fun or talk about music or football. That deeper connection is very important. Some people need to learn how to listen better to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can learn new skills, even if we are not good at them at first. Many people give praise for the final result or natural talents, like saying, "You are good at noticing details" or "You are talented at planning events." But studies show that if we praise the effort, trying new things, and solving problems, we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it found methane, which is a simple organic molecule and an important part of natural gas. Methane only lasts a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases a lot of methane at once, and the amount goes up and down with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

At the start of her job, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some hard problems. One group liked the challenge and believed they could get better. She called this a 'growth mindset.' The other group felt judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and could not see how to improve. Some of these children said they might cheat later, while others wanted to find someone who did worse than them to feel better.

Horror films like empty places. This can be an old hospital, a scary empty house, or a ghost town. Lonely places make us think. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they go away? They are very quiet, which can be scary too. Abandoned places are good for horror films because there is no phone signal there.

The basement is a scary place in horror films, no matter what kind of house it is. It is often dark and damp, and you can only get there by a narrow staircase. Basements feel creepy, even if nothing is there.

Gary Collins, a policeman on holiday, saw the London riots on TV. He recognized some people and stopped his holiday to help. He spent six months looking at CCTV videos and found 190 people, mostly by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. The facial recognition software only found one person in 200,000 hours of video.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our bodies better. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brain! Soon, we will be able to do this and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more normal.

The talk was very interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework if they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting? She also talked about how people want to be in many places at once, so they go back and forth between real-life and online chats. I see this with my daughter and her friends. They meet but sit quietly while talking to others online.

There are many news stories that make us think the world is more violent, but there is also some good news. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but most countries are living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in the last few years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, not all the news is bad. Even though violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate went down a little, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country to teach women and girls, but often these projects stop and leave them with nothing. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be stronger, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on projects in Tibet and Nepal, because in flat Bangladesh, most people have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, and people in her country and around the world are paying attention.

Many people think that developing countries are very poor and have bad leaders, with no chance for change. But this is not true. In fact, many good things are happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have earned more money and left poverty. Also, six million fewer children die from sickness each year, more girls are going to school, and many people have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback nicer by putting a negative comment between two positive ones. But if this happens all the time, workers might think the positive comments are just hiding the bad ones, making them less important. Positive feedback should help and encourage good work, not just cover up the bad.

I am part of a group that wants to stop dangerous robots. Forget the scary robots in movies. Right now, machines like drones and robots are already used to kill people with little help from humans. Soon, there may be robots that can decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this is very wrong and could be dangerous for everyone. We must be careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. But Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and learners, but there is a stronger connection between learners and the number of countries that speak the language.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about your work on the recent project. You feel worried all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by saying good things about your work on the project, and you think this is the usual way to give feedback. You know the feedback sandwich: say something nice, say what you really mean, and then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a fast rock album with catchy songs, but its lyrics are very emotional. The songs tell stories about the hard lives of regular people who feel sad and angry because they do not get rich or famous. For example, the song Glory Days is about people in a small town remembering their youth, while Downbound Train is about a young man who loses his job and his life becomes difficult. The artist seems to share real stories from his life and the lives of people he knows. This album shows how talented the Boss is.

Lewis wants more marine protected areas in the world, increasing from 3 percent to 10 percent, to help fix the damage from human activities like overfishing and pollution. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that are dying because the water is too warm and has seen empty areas in the Red Sea filled with plastic. Pugh thinks nature can heal if we give it space, but we need to act fast. If we do not take care of our seas, we might face a big problem soon.

Terrie Sharp is a popular author who tells great stories and has won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times. She grew up in a place in Glasgow with a lot of crime, where she learned to be careful and how to open car doors with a knife. Now, she uses her skills to write books and is often on TV shows like Police Today and at writing events in the UK.

Is life getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker talks about human progress and shares good news. We are living longer, healthier, and happier lives. Pinker says the real problem is that the ideas of reason and science are being attacked. When people use fear and distrust, we can hurt important things like democracy and working together in the world.

In old horror movies, when the main characters needed help, they often couldn't call for help or the police. Now, with mobile phones, this seems less real. To keep the suspense, there is no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror movie, you will probably not have signal when you really need to call for help. Or your phone battery will die right when you try to call. Or both.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their best banana, the Gros Michel, also called Big Mike. Now, the same thing is happening to the Cavendish banana, which is its replacement. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was sweet and had a thick skin, making it easy to transport. United Fruit, the biggest banana grower in South America then, grew many bananas by cloning parts of the plants instead of using seeds and planted them close together in fields.

Most spiders have venom to help them catch their food, not to hurt people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and their bites are usually not deadly. The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone since 1981 when a medicine was made to help. But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel scared, they can shoot out irritating hairs that can stick in your skin or eyes.

This scary movie idea was very popular in horror films from the late 1900s. It starts with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl almost always wins.

To understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to see how our brains are different from other animals. It is not just about brain size; we also need to know what else our brains can do and why they changed. There are not many clues about this; things left by our ancestors do not show us what they could say. However, we can see that early humans had changes in their mouth, throat, and tongue. About 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to talk.

Society tells us that girls should like arts and humanities, while boys should like maths and physics. There are not many positive female role models in science for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show scientists as men. People also think that scientists are strange and lonely. These ideas are not true, but they can make girls feel like science is not for them. If girls saw more women in science, they would feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is a free newspaper made by students and given out every week in faculty buildings. About 10,000 students read it. A survey shows that students and staff like it for fun, culture, and work experience. Printing the newspaper costs a lot. Some students cannot easily get a copy because they have to go to the university to find it. Also, many copies become litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, about 12 out of 100 employees leave their jobs each year. This number is higher than the usual 7 out of 100 in the industry. This report aims to find out why employees feel engaged at work and to suggest ways to make their work experience better and keep them in their jobs longer.

The speaker said something important. I believe that being more connected can make us feel more alone. My generation, who grew up without technology, knows how to be alone and that it's okay. But for people under 20, it's different. They talk a lot but may not know how to enjoy being alone. They also learn to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of having real conversations with people face to face.
Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always mix them, people may not value the good comments. Sometimes, just give positive feedback without adding criticism.

Your dreams can give you ideas about things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing your teeth, or being naked in public, usually have similar meanings for many people. To understand what they mean for you, try to link them to your daily experiences and feelings.

One of the most interesting examples of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets of Moscow. Some dogs were born wild, and others were pets that their owners left behind. Some dogs live alone, while others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied these dogs and found that they have adapted very well to city life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is the first novel by RJ Palacio, who lives in New York. On her website, she says the idea for the book came to her after she saw a girl with facial differences on the street. Wonder has sold many copies in the United States and has won several awards. Many schools are using it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not usual pets and has tried many times to explain that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if cared for properly. She understands why some people don’t like them because she also didn’t like rats until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how loving and smart they are. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to keep two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have died from electric shocks while playing with wires. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems with people, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to move baboons away from the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked a bit, but it is still difficult to stop baboons from returning to the city when they find easy food there.

I work for a global IT company, but their main office is in the United States, so I do my work online from home. This saves me time because I don’t have to travel or chat with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is important to me because I can take time off when my children have school events or when I need to go to the dentist. The downside is that without set working hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes miss dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti was still popular, but street art also grew a lot around the world. Some artists wanted to express political ideas and created art that made people think about war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists focused on making beautiful and attractive pieces. In South America, many street artists worked in poor neighborhoods, bringing color, life, and beauty to dull city walls.

Every day, social media, magazines, and store displays show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people often wear a few times and then throw away.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw the dust from the car going to the Big House. The horses were swatting flies with their tails and didn’t care that their owner was visiting for the first time in ten months. Sam waited because Mr. Carter only came out when he needed to, which was good for Sam. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck, and the wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was already getting red in the June sun, and he looked like a man who made money while others worked.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel, and there were strong disagreements between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council chose to take a kinder approach to deal with the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they built fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be difficult because warmer winters mean there are more pigs than before.

Suzanne was inspired to write the Hunger Games because she loves Greek mythology. When she was a child, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, the city of Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As a punishment, King Minos of Crete makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. These young people are put into a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. However, one boy named Theseus fights and kills the Minotaur. Suzanne thinks of Katniss Everdeen as a modern version of Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing together people and animals. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or left behind as pets. They also do important research on how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend called the 'buy nothing' trend is growing against consumerism. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US, where it opposes the excessive spending during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, people hold protests and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help people exchange and repair items they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police, and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils say it costs a lot to clean graffiti off buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? More and more, they see it as valuable art. Big exhibitions of street art have been held in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists by saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be valued and celebrated."

Most people have four to six dreams every night after they turn ten, which adds up to about 2,000 dreams each year. By the time they are 80 years old, an average person might have around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 percent of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand dreams in our lifetime. It’s easy to think that a dream and a real-life event can be similar, especially if the dream is about something that happens often in daily life.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor districts controlled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has complete power over the country. Each district makes different products for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, supplies all the coal for the country. There was a thirteenth district, but it fought against the Capitol in the past and was destroyed.

Wild animals often enter cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun to come into neighborhoods near the city to eat. They open trash bins and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons have even gone into people's homes to steal food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have harmed many pets, so many people in the city do not like having them around.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make mistakes, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Usually, the hero begins with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure that changes everything. In Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he discovers Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the moment that starts his adventure.

One idea to stop an asteroid heading for Earth is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. This might seem like a movie story, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon, but NASA has a real plan called the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER). They would shoot eight-ton rockets at the asteroid to try to change its path. If the asteroid is too close for this to work, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to destroy it.

Campbell says that at first, the hero does not want to go on an adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they choose to enter a special world where the adventure takes place. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, Obi-Wan is the mentor, Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO are his friends, and Darth Vader is the enemy in the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used much might seem useless to some people, but they can be valuable to others. With the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these underused items. Now, using websites and social media to buy and sell second-hand goods is easier than ever, which is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we do not know about ourselves. Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can learn about our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. The other idea was different; it said that dreams are just random brain activity while we organize our memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and create a story from them.

I am a freelancer and work for myself, which is great because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked from home, but it was hard to concentrate because there were too many distractions, like housework, tea, and my family needing my help. So, I started working at a café, but the Wi-Fi was not good and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed getting dressed for work in the morning and being able to focus in an office.

NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs if it gets the money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-metre space telescope that uses infrared light to find asteroids. If they get the money, they could reach their goal in ten years. After that, the planetary defense team would still need to figure out how to protect the planet from the really dangerous asteroids – the PHAs.

The 'buy nothing' trend has reached social media influencers who usually post about clothes and make-up to buy. Some YouTube stars now tell their viewers not to buy anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. In the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. In the next stage, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi cares a lot about religion. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions too. He becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him decide for himself about religion.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have lucid dreams. Lucid dreams are when you know you are dreaming and can control what happens in your dreams. This means you could change a scary dream into a nice one or guide your dream like a movie director. Instead of just understanding your dreams, you will be making them, but you might still want some dreams that let your mind share its thoughts!

Many people do not know they are part of the disposable clothing problem because they give their unwanted clothes to charities. However, charity shops cannot sell all these clothes. 'Fast fashion' quickly goes out of style and is often too low quality to recycle, so people do not want to buy it used. A lot of clothes are thrown away, and many that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, creating more economic and environmental issues.

Some adventurers, like Meagan McGrath from Canada, take on many challenges instead of just one trip. She has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the Sahara Desert. Her most amazing journey was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed to be rescued. Many people would have stopped there, but Meagan kept going. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sled with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls in Paris, but now he paints to make people think about social issues. He creates images of homeless people in big cities to help residents consider the problem of homelessness.

In some places, local governments have tried to stop artists from painting graffiti on random walls by giving them special areas to work in. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint and write freely. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has let some graffiti artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys visiting different places. You can see her art on sidewalks, in empty factories, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned up by city workers. For her, this shows that life is always changing with its endings and new starts.

In her last job, Gabriela worked in a culture where people respected power and authority, and everyone had their role. In this culture, leaders made important decisions and were rarely questioned. However, her Swedish team was used to a culture where employees often worked with their bosses to solve problems and make decisions. In this culture, leaders acted like coaches who encouraged independent thinking and welcomed challenges.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences between her and her team, she decided to talk to them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share their thoughts and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to take initiative and be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their jobs well. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to suggest changes to her decisions, and they explained that this was how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint many things, from small tags to large, colorful pictures of people on buildings. Their art is often very big, so they use cranes to help them. In 2007, they painted an entire castle in Scotland.

Throughout history, people have painted and written on walls. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been discovered on buildings in ancient places like Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin, including messages about religion, politics, love, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever wanted to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? If yes, you are not the only one. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike explorers in the past who used maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and travel to raise awareness about environmental problems, while others want to help people in need and raise money for charities.

The first mission is DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. They plan to test DART on the moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, called 'Didymoon', is 150 meters wide and goes around its bigger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that DART's impact will change Didymoon's path enough for telescopes on Earth to see it.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in a mining accident and needs to find food for her family. She hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very good at using a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is picked as a tribute, Katniss decides to go in her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss quickly gets into a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details, so think about the people and places in your dreams because they might be important too. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. Now you can link your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

In the past, many bridges were built from wood and were very easy to catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could sometimes set the bridge on fire and make it burn down.

We cannot know how street art will change in the future, but we can see some trends. Most street artists are young and paint in their own cities, but more are traveling and working worldwide. Some artists use the internet to communicate and share pictures of their art. The art world is also starting to accept street art as real art. Even though we don't know what will happen next, we can be sure that street art is not going away!

Suzanne Collines has always felt sad when watching news about wars. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to keep her safe by not telling her about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. This was very scary for her.

A global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) collected answers from over 40,000 millennials (born between 1983 and 1993) and non-millennials about workplace culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. Another survey by Deloitte included over 10,000 millennials who shared their views on the challenges and chances in today's work environment.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is an adventurer. He has ridden a bike in the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Remarkably, Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. Besides his travels, he helps people with disabilities to be active and takes groups of young blind people on climbing trips.

Online platforms are giving people a chance to make some extra money. For example, busy parents used to avoid selling their children's old things at local markets, but now they can easily sell baby clothes and equipment online that their kids no longer need, helping them earn some cash.

Pi and Richard Parker stay in the lifeboat for 227 days. They face hunger, sickness, and tiredness. They go through strong storms and the hot sun of the Pacific, but they manage to survive. Sometimes, Pi feels comfort from his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. Finally, they see the Mexican coast, and everything changes. It would spoil the ending to tell you more, so you should read the book to see what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. She had homework to do, but she decided to do it later. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time before her parents came home and the house became noisy with talking, the TV, or her dad listening to jazz while cooking dinner. She also liked this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's planetary defence team found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1km wide. These 'near-Earth objects' (NEOs) are as big as mountains and are located within 50 million kilometres of Earth's orbit. NASA estimates there are about 50 more to record, but says none of the 887 known NEOs are a serious threat to our planet.

Auggie decides to go to school, but his first day is very hard. Like every child starting a new school, he feels very nervous. Because of his appearance, it is even more difficult for him. No one wants to sit with him, and he sees other kids staring or whispering about him. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he talks to at lunch. However, the first day is not the only challenge. Auggie finds out that his classmates are afraid to touch him because they think he has 'the plague'. Throughout the school year, Auggie experiences many strong emotions until a surprising and upsetting event at a school camp changes everything.

The two men looked at the northern part of the land, which seemed to go on forever. They could hardly see the fences from where they were. No matter how bored a teenage boy might feel, he couldn't escape on foot. Sam watched the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground with its strong hooves. He wondered if the boy could ride. A good rider could find a lot of trouble out here, far from anyone. But someone who didn't know about horses and wanted to run away from his father might find even more trouble.

More than 4,000 climbers, aged from thirteen to eighty, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is still very dangerous, but the best climbers in the world now seek new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started to love mountain climbing when she was a teenager. After finishing school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde chose to climb all fourteen of the world's mountains that are 8,000 meters high. To make it more difficult, she climbs without oxygen tanks, which is dangerous because low oxygen at high altitudes can harm the brain and body. Gerlinde also uses her fame as a climber to help a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we think about the things we have bought in our lives, we can see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we bought even though we live in a hot country, the old smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has become a storage room.

Throughout history and in different cultures, people have believed that dreams can predict the future. They thought dreams were messages from the gods that gave us important information. Even now, many people remember dreaming about something that later happened in real life.

Many large and costly transportation projects around the world include building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross rivers, valleys, or other roads. Because of this, they are very important in civil engineering and are carefully examined, especially when they fall down.

After weeks of feeling frustrated, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the problems she had with her team. Her manager just asked if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and didn’t feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that humans often give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for everyone. Some dogs have even figured out how to use the metro to move around their area! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of places they like. Another idea is that they understand the names of stations from the announcements. Either way, people on the metro have become so used to seeing dogs on the trains that they hardly notice them anymore.

Ed Stafford from the UK was the first person to walk the whole length of the Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and reached the river's end in Brazil after two years and four months, walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always at risk. Fortunately, he only got a few thousand bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four percent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two bigger problems for society and the environment. First, many people are using credit cards to pay for these clothes. Right now, British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of what they usually spend on clothes. Also, people are spending money they don’t have to buy things they don’t need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing every year, and most of it ends up in landfills.

Ed's walk would not have been possible without technology. He used a radio to ask the rainforest people for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to help him and showed him the best paths. While walking, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the media attention from his trip to speak out against the destruction of the rainforest and to raise money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized that they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. A popular business model now is where companies create online platforms to connect customers with people who offer specific products or services. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn extra money in their free time.

One important job of modern zoos is to help with breeding programs for endangered animals. In nature, some rare animals struggle to find partners and have babies, and they face dangers from poachers, losing their homes, and other animals that hunt them. A good zoo allows these animals to live and breed safely. Also, as some wild animal numbers decrease, there is a risk that they become too similar genetically. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild to improve genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can make a bridge fall for different reasons. Trains can cause a bridge to collapse because of their speed, while boats can do it because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to prevent bridge failures is to prepare for them. New technologies that find weak spots, safer workplaces, and better designs can help reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is very scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water and knows he must climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other, until only Pi and the tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, which he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right away.

When Pi is 16, a new government is elected that his parents do not like. They are worried about the future, so they decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family travels by ship to Canada with the animals. During the journey, a big storm happens and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi ends up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a large tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults written by American author Suzanne Collins. Since it came out in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. It was also the first book for young readers to sell over a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is just as successful, making 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America!

Dreams might happen because our mind is sorting out the thoughts we have during the day, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we usually think in words, like talking to ourselves. However, when we sleep, the part of our brain that deals with language is less active, while the part that deals with emotions is more active.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. A study showed that happy people usually have strong connections with friends and family, and they spend time with them often. You also need at least one person to share your personal feelings with, which is called 'self-disclosure'. Just one close friend is enough, along with other relationships. It's not enough to have many friends just to hang out or talk about music or football; that deeper connection matters a lot. Some people need to learn how to listen better to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can learn new skills, even if we weren't good at them before. Many people often praise the final results and natural talents, like saying, "You are great at noticing details" or "You have a talent for planning events." However, studies show that if we focus on how things are done—like praising hard work, trying new things, and solving problems—we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it discovered that the air had methane, which is a simple organic molecule and an important part of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases thousands of tons of methane at once, and the amount of methane changes with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

At the start of her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some problems that were a bit too difficult for them. One group liked the challenge and believed they could improve their skills. She called this a 'growth mindset' because they focused on what they could achieve later. However, another group felt their intelligence was being judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and couldn't see how they could get better. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future, while others looked for someone who did worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films often take place in empty locations like abandoned hospitals, scary houses, or ghost towns. These lonely places make us wonder what life was like when people lived there and why they left. Their silence can also be very frightening. Plus, these places are useful for horror film directors because there is usually no phone signal there.

In horror films, basements are always scary places, no matter what type of house it is. They are often dark and damp, and you can only get to them by a narrow staircase. Something scary is usually hiding there, making basements feel creepy, even if there is nothing there.

Gary Collins, a policeman who was not working, was watching the London riots on TV. He quickly recognized some people and cut his holiday short to help identify them. He spent six months looking at CCTV footage and identified 190 people, often just by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. Even with 200,000 hours of video, facial recognition software only identified one person.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our evolution faster by improving our bodies. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brain! Soon, we will be able to do this and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory, and this idea will become more common.

The talk was very interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework when they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting at a red light? She also pointed out that people want to be in many places at once, so they keep switching between real-life and online conversations. I notice this a lot with my teenage daughter and her friends. They plan to meet but then sit quietly together, each talking online instead.

While news stories often make us think the world is becoming more violent, there is also some good news. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but countries are generally living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, the news isn't all bad for civilians. Although violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country that teach women and girls, but often these projects end and leave them with nothing. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be stronger, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on humanitarian projects in Tibet and Nepal, since most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working because people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Many people think that developing countries are in a bad state, facing extreme poverty, ruled by dictators, and having little chance for improvement. However, this is not true. In fact, a big change is happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have raised their income and escaped poverty. Also, six million fewer children die each year from sickness, more girls are going to school, and many people now have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing negative comments between two positive ones. However, if this becomes a habit, employees may see positive feedback as just a way to soften the negatives, which makes it less valuable. Positive feedback should not just be used to soften the negative but should be given to support and encourage good work.

I am part of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Instead of thinking about scary robots from movies, we should focus on what is happening now: military machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill with little human control. The next step could be robots that decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this would be very wrong and dangerous for people. We must be very careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. However, Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and learners, but there is a stronger connection between the number of learners and the number of countries where the language is spoken.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about how you did on the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by complimenting your good work on the project, and you wonder if this is just the usual nice comment before the real feedback. You know the feedback sandwich: say something nice, give the real feedback, and then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a fast and catchy rock album, but its lyrics are very emotional. The songs tell stories about the difficult lives of regular people who feel angry and disappointed because they do not achieve wealth or fame. For example, the song Glory Days is about people in a small town remembering their youth, while Downbound Train is about a young man whose life falls apart after losing his job. It seems that the artist is inspired by real people he knew and the life he could have had if he wasn't famous. This album shows the amazing talent of the Boss.

Lewis wants the number of marine protected areas in the world to grow from 3 percent to 10 percent to help fix the harm caused by human activities like overfishing, pollution, and littering. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that have lost their color because the water is too warm and has seen lifeless areas in the shallow waters of the Red Sea filled with plastic. Pugh thinks that nature can heal if we give it a chance, but time is running out. If we don't take care of our seas, we might face a big problem soon.

Terrie Sharp, a best-selling author who has won the Olive Crime Writer Award twice, knows how to tell great stories. She grew up in a tough neighborhood in Glasgow, where she learned to be careful and how to open car doors with a knife. Fortunately, she only used these skills for her writing, and now she is more active, appearing on popular daytime shows like Police Today and at writing conferences across the UK.

Is life getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker examines human progress and finds positive news. We are living longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives. Pinker believes the real issue is that the values of reason and science from the Enlightenment are being challenged. When people use tribalism, hopelessness, and distrust, we risk harming important things like democracy and global cooperation.

In older horror films, when the main characters were in trouble, they often couldn't call for help or the police. Now, with mobile phones, that seems less realistic. To keep the suspense, there is often no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror film, it is very likely that when you really need to call for help, you won't have any signal. Or your phone battery will die right when you try to call. Or both.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their most profitable product, the Gros Michel banana, also called Big Mike. Now, the same thing is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish banana. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was easy to transport, had a thick skin, and tasted sweet. United Fruit, the main banana grower and exporter in South America at that time, produced bananas very efficiently by cloning shoots from the plants instead of using seeds and growing them in crowded fields.

Most spiders have venom that helps them catch their food, not to attack people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and while their bites can hurt, they usually are not deadly. Since the anti-venom was made in 1981, the Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone. However, be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel threatened, they can release irritating hairs that can get stuck in your skin or eyes.

This common idea in horror films was very popular in the late 20th century. It begins with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl almost always wins.

To understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to examine how our brains are different from those of other animals. It's not just about brain size; we also need to consider what other functions our brains have and how they developed over time. There are very few physical clues to help us, as the tools left by our ancestors do not show us what kind of speech they could produce. However, we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early humans. By around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds, but before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

Society tells us that girls should like arts and humanities, while boys should do maths and physics. Also, there are not many positive female role models in science for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show scientists, inventors, and astronauts as men. Many people wrongly think that scientists are nerdy, have bad social skills, or work alone. These stereotypes from the media can make girls feel like they don’t belong in science and see it as an unattractive career. If girls had more positive female role models in science, it would help them feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is a free weekly newspaper for students, printed and made by students, with about 10,000 readers. A survey shows that students and staff appreciate it for fun, culture, and work experience. Printing costs a lot, and some students can't easily get a copy because they have to go to the university to find it. Also, many copies become litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, about 12 percent of employees leave each year. This may not seem like a lot, but the usual rate in the industry is 7 percent. The main goal of this report is to find out why employees are engaged at the company and to suggest ways to make their work experience better and keep them from leaving.

A lot of what the speaker said felt true. I really believe that the more connected we are, the more alone we might feel. This isn't a big problem for my generation, who have lived without technology for a long time. We know how to be alone and that it's okay to be alone. But for those under 20, it's different. They are so busy talking that they don't feel alone and might not learn to enjoy being by themselves. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of learning how to have real conversations with people face to face.

Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always mix them together, people might not appreciate the positive comments. Make sure to give positive feedback sometimes without adding any criticism.
